newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares maintain rally, up over two percent.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares maintain rally, up over two percent.

text.p: Italian shares continued their rally into the New Year on Monday buoyed by strong domestic buying interest, higher bonds and a firm lira, and supported by gains made in other world stock markets, dealers said.

Italian domestic buying was seen across a range of stocks, but international investors took a more cautious stance. Some strategists were worried about whether the sharp rises seen over the last three days could continue and were concerned that the rally had not been particularly stock selective.
The all-share Mibtel index rose 2.26 percent to 11,676 while the Mib30 was 2.24 percent higher at 17,520.

Italian stocks have been rising since last week when data for December showed a net inflow of funds into equities for the first time in two years. But dealers said these inflows must continue in January and February for the rally to be maintained.
"The market has risen so quickly over the last few days and across the board that there are some concerns this trend can be maintained," said one dealer in Milan.

Some pointed out that equity yields were attracted compared to bonds, but did not expect a massive switch as the generally cautious Italian investors still saw bonds as a safe bet, although more risky equities now offered attractive yields.
Among individual stocks, banking shares gained from the market rally with Fideuram rising 6.72 percent to 3,969 lire while Mediobanca ended up 6.14 percent at 9,642 lire.
Compart, formely Ferruzzi, was suspended limit up and was last quoted up 9.57 percent at 773 lire.
Fiat ended up 3.65 percent at 4,992 lire while Olivetti, still in talks to sell its loss-making personal computer division, was up only 0.49 percent at 613.9 percent.
